title: Integrals over the open ball of R^1 are integrals over the interval (-a, a)
statement: Let R^1 = EuclideanSpace R (Fin 1), let phi : R^1 -> R be an arbitrary function and a an arbitrary real number, and let iota(t) := EuclideanSpace.single 0 t be the vector of R^1 whose unique coordinate is t. Then the Bochner integral of phi over the open ball B_a(0) of R^1 with respect to Lebesgue measure (volume) equals the Bochner integral of t |-> phi(iota t) over the open interval (-a, a): ∫_{B_a(0)} phi = ∫_{(-a,a)} phi(iota t) dt. No integrability hypothesis is needed.
lean_statement: ∀ (φ : Rn 1 → ℝ) (a : ℝ), (∫ y in ball (0 : Rn 1) a, φ y) = ∫ t in Ioo (-a) a, φ (EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 1) t)
